architecture.title: How Axentra fits together
architecture.caption: Studio and your own application use the same HTTP API. The server keeps all data in PostgreSQL, stores file contents in the configured file storage and sends webhooks and notifications through its background worker.
architecture.studioDetail: Admin UI in the browser, signed in with a user session
architecture.appDetail: Backend or service, authenticates with an API key (SDK or HTTP)
architecture.serverDetail: Identity, access, data, files, events and jobs, usage, billing, notifications, audit
architecture.databaseDetail: All records, settings and audit entries; tenants isolated by row-level security
architecture.outboundDetail: Webhooks, email and payment provider calls from the background worker

hierarchy.title: Platform, products and tenants
hierarchy.caption: Each product is an isolated app on the platform. Tenants belong to exactly one product. User accounts belong to the platform and become members of products and tenants with a role.
hierarchy.platformDetail: User accounts, platform admins, server settings
hierarchy.productDetail: Settings, operators, roles, API keys, plans, templates, webhooks
hierarchy.users: User accounts belong to the platform. A user becomes a product operator (product role, covers all tenants) or a tenant member (tenant role); one person can hold several memberships. API keys belong to a product and can be bound to one tenant.

jobLifecycle.title: Job states
jobLifecycle.caption: A job is queued, picked up by a worker and either succeeds or ends in one of the outcomes below.
jobLifecycle.runningDetail: A worker holds a lease and runs the handler
jobLifecycle.retryDetail: Temporary error or expired lease while attempts remain; waits for the backoff delay
jobLifecycle.cancelledDetail: Cancellation was requested while the job was queued or running
jobLifecycle.manualRetry: Retry puts a failed or dead job back into the queue and resets its attempt count to 0.

webhookDelivery.title: Webhook deliveries
webhookDelivery.caption: Every matching event creates one delivery per endpoint. Each attempt is an HTTPS POST signed with the endpoint's signing secret.
webhookDelivery.match: enabled endpoints with matching event types and tenant filter
webhookDelivery.failedDetail: Error, timeout or non-2xx response; retried after a backoff delay
webhookDelivery.deadDetail: Attempts used up, URL refused or endpoint disabled
webhookDelivery.redeliver: Redeliver sends a finished delivery again (not while it is pending). A test ping is sent once and ends as delivered or dead.

keyRotation.title: Rotating an API key with a grace period
keyRotation.caption: Rotation creates a new key (new ID and secret; same name, permissions, tenant and expiry). The old key keeps working until the grace period ends (0 seconds to 7 days) and is then revoked. Keys derived from the old key are not affected.
